Okay so this is going to be a slightly longer post, but I wanted to explain why we decided to stop offering a free trial after four years, because a lot of people assumed it was about money when really it was about the kind of customers the trial was attracting and how much of our support time they were eating up every single week.

Bear with me because this one is a bit long, but last year I left a $180k job to work on my own product, and after twelve months of building, launching and mostly failing, the thing that surprised me most was not the money or the stress, it was how lonely the whole thing turned out to be when nobody around you is doing the same.

Okay this might be a long one but I think it matters: we spent two years building the features our customers asked for and churn barely moved, then we spent three months fixing onboarding and churn dropped by almost half, which taught me that what customers ask for and what they need are rarely the same thing.
